sources.note: Nothing: phonemes (§2), syllable CyVN/T (§3), eight tones (§4); no occurrence of 'stress' or 'accent'. And the dialect is the Black Miao of the Qingshui-jiang river (Shidong/Taigong; Li Fang-Kuei's 1941 data) = Qiandong (Hmu) Miao, not Mashan; Glottolog itself marks the hmw link as 'possibly'.

sources.citation: Lam, Man Fong. 2026. Phonation as a Cue to Tone Splits in Central Mashan Hmong. Abstract ID 413, Linguistics 2026 Paris (1 p.).
sources.note: Nothing on stress; Central Mashan (Zongdi, Ziyun) has 11-13 tones with phonation cues. Sister variety, not hmw.

No stress statement. Western Mang = Sidazhai, Houchang Twp, Ziyun (10,000+); 'Most Central Mang and Western Mang dialects have eleven to thirteen tones' (odd-numbered tones split); cites Wang 1985, Li Yunbing 2000/2018, Wu & Yang 2010, Heal 2020.

sources.citation: 维基百科. 苗语麻山次方言 (wikitext, accessed 2026-09-17).
sources.note: No stress statement. 西部土语 = 紫云县猴场镇、四大寨乡, 1.4万人; tone splitting of tones 1/3/5/7 by old aspiration gives 12 tone classes in Central and Western; refs Wang 1985, Li 2000, Li 2018, Sun & Ting 2017, Wu & Yang 2010.

sources.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2010. Hmong-Mien Language History. Pacific Linguistics 613. Canberra: ANU. 310 pp.
sources.note: Family-level comparative work (Zongdi = Central Mashan is a data point). The only word-stress passage (p. 28, §2.1.3.2 point 4) quotes Downer 1961:539 on Mien reduced syllables having 'weaker stress and shorter duration than the following full syllables so that a strong iambic rhythm is imparted to disyllabic words'; nothing on Hmongic or Mashan word stress.
